description: Cat clone with syntax highlighting and Git integration.

next.name: cache
tip: Modify the syntax-definition and theme cache.

option.name: --acknowledgements
tip: Build acknowledgements.bin.
Requires --build.

option.name: --blank
tip: Create completely new syntax and theme sets (instead of appending to the default sets).
Requires --build.

option.name: --build
tip: Initialize (or update) the syntax/theme cache.
Loads from the source directory (default: the configuration directory).

option.name: --clear
tip: Remove the cached syntax definitions and themes.

option.name: --source
tip: Use a different directory to load syntaxes and themes from.
Requires --build.

option.name: --target
tip: Use a different directory to store the cached syntax and theme set.
Requires --build.

option.name: --acknowledgements
tip: Show acknowledgements.

option.name: --binary
tip: How to treat binary content (default: no-printing).

option.name: --cache-dir
tip: Show bat's cache directory.

option.name: --chop-long-lines
tip: Truncate all lines longer than screen width.
Alias for '--wrap=never'.

option.name: --color
tip: Specify when to use colored output.
The automatic mode only enables colors if an interactive terminal is detected - colors are automatically disabled if the output goes to a pipe.

option.name: --completion
tip: Show shell completion for a certain shell.
Possible values: bash, fish, ps1, zsh

option.name: --config-dir
tip: Show bat's configuration directory.

option.name: --config-file
tip: Show path to the configuration file.

option.name: --decorations
tip: Specify when to use the decorations that have been specified via '--style'.
The automatic mode only enables decorations if an interactive terminal is detected.
The always mode will show decorations even when piping output.

option.name: --diagnostics
tip: Show diagnostic information for bug reports.

option.name: --diff
tip: Only show lines that have been added/removed/modified with respect to the Git index.
Use --diff-context=N to control how much context you want to see.

option.name: --diff-context
tip: Include N lines of context around added/removed/modified lines when using '--diff'.

option.name: --file-name
tip: Specify the name to display for a file.
Useful when piping data to bat from STDIN when bat does not otherwise know the filename.
Note that the provided file name is also used for syntax detection.

option.name: --force-colorization
tip: Alias for '--decorations=always --color=always'.
This is useful if the output of bat is piped to another program, but you want to keep the colorization/decorations.

option.name: --generate-config-file
tip: Generates a default configuration file.

option.name: --help
tip: Print help information.

option.name: --highlight-line
tip: Highlight the specified line ranges with a different background color.

option.name: --ignored-suffix
tip: Ignore extension.

option.name: --italic-text
tip: Specify when to use ANSI sequences for italic text in the output.

option.name: --language
tip: Explicitly set the language for syntax highlighting.
The language can be specified as a name (like 'C++' or 'LaTeX') or possible file extension (like 'cpp', 'hpp' or 'md').
Use '--list-languages' to show all supported language names and file extensions.

option.name: --line-range
tip: Only print the specified range of lines for each file.

example.desc: prints lines 40 to the end of the file

option.name: --list-languages
tip: Display a list of supported languages for syntax highlighting.

option.name: --list-themes
tip: Display a list of supported themes for syntax highlighting.

option.name: --map-syntax
tip: Map a glob pattern to an existing syntax name.
The glob pattern is matched on the full path and the filename.
Note that the right-hand side is the *name* of the syntax, not a file extension.

example.desc: highlight *.build files with the Python syntax
highlight files named '.myignore' with the Git Ignore syntax

option.name: --no-config
tip: Do not use the configuration file.

option.name: --no-custom-assets
tip: Do not load custom assets.

option.name: --no-paging
tip: Alias for '--paging=never'.

option.name: --nonprintable-notation
tip: Set notation for non-printable characters.

option.name: --number
tip: Only show line numbers, no other decorations.
This is an alias for '--style=numbers'.

option.name: --pager
tip: Determine which pager is used.
This option will override the PAGER and BAT_PAGER environment variables.
The default pager is 'less'.

option.name: --paging
tip: Specify when to use the pager.
To disable the pager, use '--paging=never' or its alias, '-P'.
To disable the pager permanently, set BAT_PAGING to 'never'.

option.name: --plain
tip: Only show plain style, no decorations.
When '-p' is used twice ('-pp'), it also disables automatic paging.

option.name: --set-terminal-title
tip: Sets terminal title to filenames when using a pager.

option.name: --show-nonprintable
tip: Show non-printable characters like space, tab or newline.
This option can also be used to print binary files.
Use '--tabs' to control the width of the tab-placeholders.

option.name: --squeeze-blank
tip: Squeeze consecutive empty lines into a single empty line.

option.name: --squeeze-limit
tip: Set the maximum number of consecutive empty lines to be printed.

option.name: --strip-ansi
tip: Specify when to strip ANSI escape sequences from the input.
The automatic mode will remove escape sequences unless the syntax highlighting language is plain text.

option.name: --style
tip: Configure which elements to display in addition to the file contents.
The argument is a comma-separated list of components to display (e.g. 'numbers,changes,grid') or a pre-defined style ('full').

option.name: --tabs
tip: Set the tab width to T spaces.
Use a width of 0 to pass tabs through directly.

option.name: --terminal-width
tip: Explicitly set the width of the terminal instead of determining it automatically.
If prefixed with '+' or '-', the value will be treated as an offset to the actual terminal width.

option.name: --theme
tip: Set the theme for syntax highlighting.
Use '--list-themes' to see all available themes.

option.name: --theme-dark
tip: Sets the theme name for syntax highlighting used when the terminal uses a dark background.

option.name: --theme-light
tip: Sets the theme name for syntax highlighting used when the terminal uses a light background.

option.name: --unbuffered
tip: This option exists for POSIX-compliance reasons ('u' is for 'unbuffered').
The output is always unbuffered - this option is simply ignored.

option.name: --version
tip: Print version.

option.name: --wrap
tip: Specify the text-wrapping mode (*auto*, never, character).
The '--terminal-width' option can be used in addition to control the output width.
